title: Your algo can have positive expectancy and still blow up. Position sizing is the part nobody backtests properly
author: socialwhizca
selftext:
Learned this the expensive way. You can have a genuinely profitable system, positive expectancy, good win rate, and still hit zero, if your position sizing lets a normal losing streak drain the account. Expectancy tells you the long-run average; risk of ruin tells you whether you survive to get there.

The math people skip: even a 60% win-rate system will have runs of 6-8 losers eventually, it's just probability. If each trade risks 5% of capital, an 8-loss streak is a 40% drawdown you may never recover from. Same system at 1% risk barely notices it. The edge didn't change, the survival did.

So before optimizing your entry logic for the 100th time, model your risk of ruin across realistic losing streaks and size so a bad run is survivable, not fatal. (Also, model it on live-realistic costs, my drawdowns ran deeper live on AvaTrade than backtest until I stopped assuming perfect fills and zero slippage.)

For the algo folks: do you size fixed-fractional, Kelly, something custom? And did under-sizing or over-sizing hurt you more early on?
